summary: Critical errors exist including completely masked failures, severe file descriptor and interval leaks, and potential path traversal vulnerabilities.

findings.title: Silent failure masking in runOne
findings.body: The catch block in `runOne` unconditionally returns `{ id, ok: true }` when an exception is caught. This masks all failures (such as the 1MB log limit or I/O errors) and incorrectly reports failed jobs as successful.
findings.recommendation: Return `{ id, ok: false }` along with the error detail in the catch block.

findings.title: File descriptor leak on job execution
findings.body: `runOne` opens a file handle via `openJob` but never closes it. Additionally, `openJob` leaves the handle open if it throws the file size error. This will exhaust system file descriptors (EMFILE) and crash the application.
findings.recommendation: Close the handle in `openJob` before throwing, and ensure `runOne` calls `await handle.close()` inside a `finally` block.

findings.title: Unstoppable interval and unhandled promise rejection in heartbeat
findings.body: `startHeartbeat` creates a continuous interval without returning the interval ID, making it impossible to stop. Furthermore, it calls `fs.appendFile` (which returns a Promise in node:fs/promises) without `.catch()`, causing unhandled promise rejections on I/O failures.
findings.recommendation: Return the interval ID from `startHeartbeat` so it can be cleared, and add a `.catch()` block to `fs.appendFile` to safely handle I/O failures.

findings.title: Path traversal vulnerability
findings.body: The `id` parameter is directly interpolated into the file path (`/var/jobs/${id}.log`). If `id` is user-provided, it allows an attacker to append data to arbitrary files via directory traversal (e.g. `../../../etc/passwd`).
findings.recommendation: Sanitize the `id` variable (e.g., validate it against a strict alphanumeric regex) or safely construct the path using `path.basename(id)`.

samples.summary: Severe resource leaks, silent error masking, and path traversal vulnerabilities detected.

findings.title: Silent error masking in runOne
findings.body: The catch block in `runOne` returns `{ id, ok: true }` regardless of the error thrown (e.g., file too large, I/O errors). This completely masks failures and falsely reports success to the caller.
findings.recommendation: Return `{ id, ok: false, error: err }` or rethrow the error in the catch block.

findings.title: File descriptor leak in openJob and runOne
findings.body: File handles opened with `fs.open` are stored in a global `handles` map but are never closed. If the file size check throws an error, the open handle is immediately leaked. Furthermore, there is no mechanism to close handles when a job completes successfully.
findings.recommendation: Call `await handle.close()` before throwing the size error, and implement a cleanup mechanism to close file handles once jobs complete.

findings.title: Unstoppable interval leak in startHeartbeat
findings.body: `startHeartbeat` creates a periodic interval using `setInterval` but does not store or return the resulting interval ID. This creates an unreferenced background task that will run indefinitely, keeping the Node process alive and continuously performing disk I/O.
findings.recommendation: Return the interval ID from `startHeartbeat` so the caller can execute `clearInterval` when the heartbeat is no longer needed.

findings.title: Path traversal vulnerability
findings.body: The `id` parameter is unsafely interpolated directly into file paths. If `id` originates from untrusted input, an attacker could supply payloads like `../../../etc/passwd` to perform arbitrary file writes/appends outside the intended `/var/jobs/` directory.
findings.recommendation: Validate and sanitize the `id` parameter to ensure it only contains safe characters (e.g., strictly alphanumeric or UUID format) before using it in file paths.

findings.recommendation: Validate `id` against a strict allowlist regex (e.g., alphanumeric/UUID) or use `path.basename(id)` before constructing the file path.

findings.recommendation: Return the timer ID from `startHeartbeat` to allow for proper cleanup (`clearInterval`), and add a `.catch()` block to handle `fs.appendFile` errors.
